q_en: How does the writer join one idea to the next?
not_yet: Why a word after وَ copies the one before: later.
Joiners that need a pronoun on them: later.
Using joiners to build long texts: Stage 5 reading.
not_yet_ar: لِمَاذَا تُشْبِهُ الْكَلِمَةُ بَعْدَ الْوَاوِ حَرَكَةَ مَا قَبْلَهَا: فِي وَقْتٍ لَاحِقٍ.
كَلِمَاتُ الرَّبْطِ الَّتِي يَتَّصِلُ بِهَا ضَمِيرٌ: فِي وَقْتٍ لَاحِقٍ.
الرَّبْطُ فِي النُّصُوصِ الطَّوِيلَةِ: فِي دُرُوسِ الْقِرَاءَةِ.

lines: Which small words sit between two ideas?
أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ صَغِيرَةٍ تَقَعُ بَيْنَ فِكْرَتَيْنِ؟
Which stick to the next word? Which stand alone?
Does a joiner change the next word’s kind?
هَلْ تُغَيِّرُ كَلِمَةُ الرَّبْطِ نَوْعَ الْكَلِمَةِ؟

slides.head_en: Two joiners stick to the next word

cards.def_en: the next thing follows at once

slides.note: The joiner is not the main word: the word after it keeps its own kind.
slides.note_ar: كَلِمَةُ الرَّبْطِ لَيْسَتْ هِيَ الْأَصْلَ: الْكَلِمَةُ بَعْدَهَا تَبْقَى عَلَى نَوْعِهَا.

rows: came in, and at once sat
slides.tip: Both mean “then”. فَ = straight away. ثُمَّ = after a while.
slides.tip_ar: كِلَاهُمَا بِمَعْنَى “then” بِالْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةِ: فَ مُبَاشَرَةً، وَثُمَّ بَعْدَ مُدَّةٍ.

slides.head_en: Look: the kind does not change
sents: The boy sat and read a muṣḥaf.
Ahmad and Umar went to the ribāṭ.
The boy left, then came back.

slides.small: وَ and فَ are written as part of the next word, but they are small particles: read them as “and” and “so”.
slides.small_ar: الْوَاوُ وَالْفَاءُ تُكْتَبَانِ مَعَ الْكَلِمَةِ التَّالِيَةِ لَكِنَّهُمَا حَرْفَانِ.

slides.why: Sara wrote وَ on its own. Wrong! The joiners وَ and فَ are always joined to the next word: وَجَلَسَ. (Only ثُمَّ، أَوْ، لَكِنْ، بَلْ stand alone.)
slides.why_ar: خَطَأٌ! الْوَاوُ وَالْفَاءُ تَلْتَصِقَانِ بِالْكَلِمَةِ التَّالِيَةِ: وَجَلَسَ.

can: I can read the six joiners (وَ فَ ثُمَّ أَوْ لَكِنْ بَلْ) and say what each one means.
I can see that attached وَ and فَ are particles, while the word keeps its own kind.

أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَرَى أَنَّ الْوَاوَ وَالْفَاءَ حَرْفَانِ وَأَنَّ الْكَلِمَةَ تَبْقَى عَلَى نَوْعِهَا.

lines: A boy went to a mosque.
The boy sat in the mosque.
The boy opened a muṣḥaf (a copy of the Qur’an).
The boy read in the muṣḥaf.
The boy sat in the study circle.
The friends went to the mosque.
The students read in the books.

The Habib is a righteous man.
Is the Habib in the mosque?
